input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: § 7.2 is a reverse MFN burdening us: it obliges Customer, before engaging another provider, to disclose any more favourable commercial offer it receives and match it for Vendor. That is an open-ended obligation to extend better third-party terms to Vendor, which is the walk-away position under the MFN rule (MFN is only acceptable in Customer's favour). It also directly conflicts with § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment. No Vendor-granted MFN exists elsewhere in the document, so deleting § 7.2 is the minimal edit reaching the preferred position.

proposal.summary: Delete reverse MFN in § 7.2 requiring Customer to disclose and match third-party offers
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted § 7.2 because it runs the wrong way: it would oblige us to disclose our other commercial offers and match them for Vendor, which our playbook does not accept, and it contradicts § 12.3 where Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. If Vendor needs something here, we can consider an MFN in our favour, or at most a matching right limited to a defined product for 12 months with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
